title: CMAKE: Fix ENABLE_ASAN for MSVC
description:
Problem:
- SPECTRE-mitigation (/Qspectre) is enabled by default but this does not allow
ASAN (-fsanitize=address) to be enabled because of failing compiler checks for
ASAN_FLAG. This problem can also be reproduced with a C++ console application
sample using Visual Studio 2019/2022 where it will report linking error related
to ASAN library if both the options are enabled.

Cause:
- This happens because the ASAN libraries are not present in the path that is
used by the linker when SPECTRE-mitigation is enabled.
- ASAN libraries are present in VS_TOOLSET_PATH/lib/<arch> but are not present
in VS_TOOLSET_PATH/lib/spectre/<arch> which is the path used by
SPECTRE-mitigation libraries.
- Following links also talk about the same problem.
https://github.com/MarkSchofield/WindowsToolchain/issues/72
https://github.com/MarkSchofield/WindowsToolchain/issues/73

Fixes:
- First fix is to disable SPECTRE-mitigation when ASAN is requested and is
considered a default fix by this change.
- Second fix is to add path where ASAN libraries are present and is activated
only when ENABLE_ASAN_WITH_SPECTRE is provided on the CMake command line along
with ENABLE_ASAN.

Note:
- Both the fixes are applicable for Debug and RelWithDebInfo build types only
because they provide the necessary debug information required for ASAN to be
functional. If ASAN is enabled on Release and MinSizeRel build types too, then
warning C5072 gets generated causing build failure (because this warning is
treated as an error).

Example:
- error C2220: the following warning is treated as an error
- warning C5072: ASAN enabled without debug information emission.
                 Enable debug info for better ASAN error reporting.

Important:
- Checking if ASAN is supported requires SPECTRE-mitigation to be disabled
globally impacting all build types. If ASAN is supported, then it is re-enabled
selectively depending on the build types.
- As per /libpath documentation, path provided to it is used before all the
other paths. This causes SPECTRE-mitigated libraries to be skipped if
non-mitigated versions are present in the ASAN library path. For example,
comsuppw.lib is present in both the paths. If SPECTRE-mitigation is enabled
(along with ASAN), and only ASAN library path is added, then comsuppw.lib from
ASAN library path is used!

Summary:
- For First or Default Fix
  - Debug and RelWithDebInfo: SPECTRE-mitigation stays disabled
                              ASAN is enabled
  - Release and MinSizeRel: SPECTRE-mitigation is re-enabled
                            ASAN is skipped
- For Second Fix
  - Debug and RelWithDebInfo: SPECTRE-mitigation is re-enabled
                              ASAN is enabled
  - Release and MinSizeRel: SPECTRE-mitigation is re-enabled
                            ASAN is skipped

**Testing ASAN (with this change)**

1. **Clear Build Directory**

   ```
   cd .. && rd /q /s wsbuild64 && md wsbuild64 && cd wsbuild64
   ```
2. **Build with ASAN Enabled**

   ```
   To Build with Fix #1 (SPECTRE Disabled and ASAN Enabled)
   cmake -G "Visual Studio 17 2022" -A x64 ..\wireshark -DENABLE_ASAN=ON --fresh
   
   OR
   
   To Build with Fix #2 (SPECTRE Enabled and ASAN Enabled)
   cmake -G "Visual Studio 17 2022" -A x64 ..\wireshark -DENABLE_ASAN=ON -DENABLE_ASAN_WITH_SPECTRE=ON --fresh
   
   In both the scenarios, ASAN is enabled for Debug and RelDebWithInfo build types only.
   ```
3. **Launch Wireshark Solution in Visual Studio 2022 for Manual Checks**

   ```
   Wireshark.sln
   
   Check for "Enable Address Sanitizer" and "Spectre Mitigation" under "C/C++ -> All Options" and "Command Line" under "Linker" for wireshark project properties.
   
   When only ENABLE_ASAN=ON is used,
                    Enable-Address-Sanitizer  Spectre-Mitigation  Linker-Command-Line
   Debug            /fsanitize=address        Disabled            (no changes)
   RelWithDebInfo   -"-                       -"-                 -"-
   Release          No                        Enabled (/Qspectre) -"-
   MinSizeRel       -"-                       -"-                 -"-
   
   When ENABLE_ASAN=ON and ENABLE_ASAN_WITH_SPECTRE=ON is used,
                    Enable-Address-Sanitizer  Spectre-Mitigation    Linker-Command-Line
   Debug            /fsanitize=address        Enabled (/Qspectre)   with spectre-n-asan lib paths
   RelWithDebInfo   -"-                       -"-                   -"-
   Release          No                        -"-                   without spectre-n-asan lib paths
   MinSizeRel       -"-                       -"-                   -"-
   ```
4. **Add Crashing Code**

   ```note
   Add "dns_qr_r_ra_ttls[TTL_MAXIMUM_ELEMENTS] = 0;" inside dns_stats_tree_init().
   
   Line 5119 static void dns_stats_tree_init(stats_tree* st)
   Line 5120 {
   Line 5121   dns_qr_r_ra_ttls[TTL_MAXIMUM_ELEMENTS] = 0;
   ```
5. **Build Debug, RelWithDebInfo, Release and MinSizeRel Build Types**

   ```
   msbuild /m /p:Configuration=Debug Wireshark.sln /t:Clean;Rebuild
   msbuild /m /p:Configuration=RelWithDebInfo Wireshark.sln /t:Clean;Rebuild
   msbuild /m /p:Configuration=Release Wireshark.sln /t:Clean;Rebuild
   msbuild /m /p:Configuration=MinSizeRel Wireshark.sln /t:Clean;Rebuild
   ```

**SPECTRE and ASAN Test Results for `/libpath`**

Following tests were conducted using a [sample COM program](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/wmisdk/example--getting-wmi-data-from-the-local-computer?redirectedfrom=MSDN) to show the impact of SPECTRE and ASAN options on how the linker uses library path to find and link ASAN library and to find-n-link with `comsuppw.lib` which is present in both the directories.

Default Library Path _(which includes ASAN libraries too)_: `C:\Program Files\Microsoft Visual Studio\2022\Professional\VC\Tools\MSVC\14.39.33519\lib\x64\comsuppw.lib`

SPECTRE-mitigated Library Path: `C:\Program Files\Microsoft Visual Studio\2022\Professional\VC\Tools\MSVC\14.39.33519\lib\spectre\x64\comsuppw.lib`

\-

**Test 1:** SPECTRE Disabled and ASAN Disabled _(results are as expected)_

`link.exe CreateFile SUCCESS C:\Program Files\Microsoft Visual Studio\2022\Professional\VC\Tools\MSVC\14.39.33519\lib\x64\comsuppw.lib`

> Since SPECTRE and ASAN, both are disabled, the linker uses the default library path for finding and linking with `comsuppw.lib`.

\-

**Test 2:** SPECTRE Enabled and ASAN Disabled _(results are as expected)_

`link.exe CreateFile SUCCESS C:\Program Files\Microsoft Visual Studio\2022\Professional\VC\Tools\MSVC\14.39.33519\lib\spectre\x64\comsuppw.lib`

> Since only SPECTRE is enabled, the linker uses the SPECTRE-mitigated library path for finding and linking with `comsuppw.lib`.

\-

**Test 3:** SPECTRE Disabled and ASAN Enabled _(results are as expected)_

`link.exe CreateFile SUCCESS C:\Program Files\Microsoft Visual Studio\2022\Professional\VC\Tools\MSVC\14.39.33519\lib\x64\comsuppw.lib`

> Since only ASAN is enabled, the linker uses the default library path for finding and linking with the ASAN library along with `comsuppw.lib`.

\-

**Test 4:** SPECTRE Enabled and ASAN Enabled _(results are as expected)_

`LINK : fatal error LNK1104: cannot open file 'clang_rt.asan_dynamic_runtime_thunk-x86_64.lib' above happens because ASAN libraries are not present inside lib\spectre\x64 which is where the linker searches for it`

> Since both the options, SPECTRE and ASAN are enabled, the linker uses the SPECTRE-mitigated library path to find and link with the ASAN library. But since it is not present there _(and present only in the default library path)_, it results in failure.

\-

**Test 5:** SPECTRE Enabled and ASAN Enabled (with `/libpath:<default library path>`) _(results ARE NOT as expected)_

`link.exe CreateFile SUCCESS C:\Program Files\Microsoft Visual Studio\2022\Professional\VC\Tools\MSVC\14.39.33519\lib\x64\comsuppw.lib`

> Since `/libpath:<default library path>` was provided, the linker used it to find and link with the ASAN library but also used the same path to link with `comsuppw.lib` instead of picking from `lib\spectre\x64`. And this is expected because the linker uses the path provided in `/libpath:<>` prior to any other paths but is a cause of concern because SPECTRE-mitigated libraries will then NOT BE used even though being present.

\-

**Test 6:** SPECTRE Enabled and ASAN Enabled (with `/libpath:<default library path>` `/libpath:<spectre-mitigated library path>`) _(results ARE NOT as expected)_

`link.exe CreateFile SUCCESS C:\Program Files\Microsoft Visual Studio\2022\Professional\VC\Tools\MSVC\14.39.33519\lib\x64\comsuppw.lib`

> Even though SPECTRE-mitigated library path was added, its order is equally important. In this case, since it is provided after the default library path, it results in the same problem as seen in test 5.

\-

**Test 7:** SPECTRE Enabled and ASAN Enabled (with `/libpath:<spectre-mitigated library path>` `/libpath:<default library path>`) _(results are as expected)_

`link.exe CreateFile SUCCESS C:\Program Files\Microsoft Visual Studio\2022\Professional\VC\Tools\MSVC\14.39.33519\lib\spectre\x64\comsuppw.lib`

> In this test, the library path order has SPECTRE-mitigated library path prior to default library path which is the correct order allowing SPECTRE and ASAN both to work as expected. This library path order is used in the second fix when ENABLE_ASAN_WITH_SPECTRE is provided.

I think this might be a bit _too_ thorough. Is there any reason why we shouldn't simply disable `/Qspectre` if `ENABLE_ASAN` is true and not worry about `ENABLE_ASAN_WITH_SPECTRE`? Enabling ASAN implies that you're testing and likely not worried about spectre mitigations.

I agree, hence initially started with SPECTRE-mitigation disabled but then realized that, if for some reason, developers want it enabled along with ASAN functionality, then they have to add those library paths and in that particular order. This will require them to either use Visual Studio or touch `CMakeLists.txt`, both of which could be tricky if they are not aware as to where _(and possibly how)_ they need to make those changes.

@geraldcombs - Do you want the additional bits to be removed? _(but it would cut down only the `if(ENABLE_ASAN_WITH_SPECTRE)` block)_. The other option would be to trim the comments _(leaving a link to this merge request for documentation purpose)_ to make the changes look compact.
Apologies for the delay in responding. I think trimming down the comments and linking to this MR for more details would make sense.

Thanks @geraldcombs for the suggestion. I have removed the 2 new comment blocks and added the merge request link for more details.

+		message(FATAL_ERROR "ENABLE_ASAN_WITH_SPECTRE was requested, but without ENABLE_ASAN!")
+	endif()
+endif()
+
 if(ENABLE_TSAN)
 	# Available since Clang >= 3.2 and GCC >= 4.8
 	cmake_push_check_state()

commits_data.title: CMAKE: Fix ENABLE_ASAN for MSVC
commits_data.message:
CMAKE: Fix ENABLE_ASAN for MSVC

Problem:
- SPECTRE-mitigation (/Qspectre) is enabled by default but this does not allow
ASAN (-fsanitize=address) to be enabled because of failing compiler checks for
ASAN_FLAG. This problem can also be reproduced with a C++ console application
sample using Visual Studio 2019/2022 where it will report linking error related
to ASAN library if both the options are enabled.

Cause:
- This happens because the ASAN libraries are not present in the path that is
used by the linker when SPECTRE-mitigation is enabled.
- ASAN libraries are present in VS_TOOLSET_PATH/lib/<arch> but are not present
in VS_TOOLSET_PATH/lib/spectre/<arch> which is the path used by
SPECTRE-mitigation libraries.
- Following links also talk about the same problem.
https://github.com/MarkSchofield/WindowsToolchain/issues/72
https://github.com/MarkSchofield/WindowsToolchain/issues/73

Fixes:
- First fix is to disable SPECTRE-mitigation when ASAN is requested and is
considered a default fix by this change.
- Second fix is to add path where ASAN libraries are present and is activated
only when ENABLE_ASAN_WITH_SPECTRE is provided on the CMake command line along
with ENABLE_ASAN.

Note:
- Both the fixes are applicable for Debug and RelWithDebInfo build types only
because they provide the necessary debug information required for ASAN to be
functional. If ASAN is enabled on Release and MinSizeRel build types too, then
warning C5072 gets generated causing build failure (because this warning is
treated as an error).

Example:
- error C2220: the following warning is treated as an error
- warning C5072: ASAN enabled without debug information emission.
                 Enable debug info for better ASAN error reporting.

Important:
- Checking if ASAN is supported requires SPECTRE-mitigation to be disabled
globally impacting all build types. If ASAN is supported, then it is re-enabled
selectively depending on the build types.
- As per /libpath documentation, path provided to it is used before all the
other paths. This causes SPECTRE-mitigated libraries to be skipped if
non-mitigated versions are present in the ASAN library path. For example,
comsuppw.lib is present in both the paths. If SPECTRE-mitigation is enabled
(along with ASAN), and only ASAN library path is added, then comsuppw.lib from
ASAN library path is used!

Summary:
- For First or Default Fix
  - Debug and RelWithDebInfo: SPECTRE-mitigation stays disabled
                              ASAN is enabled
  - Release and MinSizeRel: SPECTRE-mitigation is re-enabled
                            ASAN is skipped
- For Second Fix
  - Debug and RelWithDebInfo: SPECTRE-mitigation is re-enabled
                              ASAN is enabled
  - Release and MinSizeRel: SPECTRE-mitigation is re-enabled
                            ASAN is skipped
